name: How do I know if a whole-home renovation quote is too low?

mainEntity.name: What warning signs show that a whole-home renovation bid is unrealistically low?
mainEntity.text: What warning signs show that a whole-home renovation bid is unrealistically low?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unrealistically low bids usually omit important pieces of the project. Common red flags include vague descriptions, very low allowances, no mention of permits, no allowance for structural or system upgrades, and unclear exclusions. A contractor may be trying to win the job by pricing only visible work while assuming changes will be handled later as extras. That can create conflict once construction begins. Compare at least two or three detailed bids and look for consistency in scope. If one number is dramatically lower, ask exactly what is missing. The best bid is not the cheapest one; it is the one that most accurately reflects the real work required.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bid may be too low if it lacks detailed scope, uses vague allowances, excludes permits or engineering, or is far below comparable proposals. An unusually cheap quote often signals missing work, not a genuine savings opportunity.
